1.d4 Nf6 2.Nf3 g6 3.Bg5 Bg7 4.Nbd2 d5 5..strategy: Backs d4 and opens the king's bishop, accepting a slower, closed game now that d5 has stopped e4. White's pieces are well placed for a patient fight, with the bishop on g5 still out in front of the pawn chain.

Castles and puts the king behind the fianchettoed bishop. The pawn on d5 holds the centre, so Black can challenge White's from the flank, and a trade of the g5 bishop for the f6 knight would hand Black both bishops.
